judged_text: The rewritten Google Meet fallback dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar without optional chaining, so it throws TypeError when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty — exactly the 'Google Meet selected w/o a Google Cal' case this branch exists to handle (the old code used evt.destinationCalendar?.integration and safely fell back to Daily). Any booking created or rescheduled with a Google Meet location while no destination calendar resolves (handleNewBooking sets destinationCalendar to null in that case, and confirm.handler sets it to []) crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' and fails with a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video; no test in the diff triggers this branch.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new Google Meet fallback does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then unconditionally dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`, destructuring yields `mainHostDestinationCalendar === undefined`, so `.integration` throws a TypeError. The diff also shows call sites that can produce `null`/empty arrays (e.g. `handleNewBooking` sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` when none, and `confirm.handler.ts` sets it to `[]`), matching the exact scenario this fallback is meant to handle.
